name: BLSA
notes: Oldest US longitudinal aging study. NIA-funded. Includes amyloid PET.
access_requirements: Researchers in the US and abroad are welcome. You submit a pre-analysis plan (decision in 4–6 weeks), then an analysis plan; reviews run about every 4 weeks. A BLSA scientist is assigned and should be a co-author. The NIA must approve abstracts and manuscripts before submission. Publications must stay within the approved aims, and misuse bars you from further access.
percent_women_source: AI2D harmonised MRI subset 52.6% (n=1,152), not whole cohort [https://pennlinc.github.io/AI2D/docs/datasets/BLSA]
womens_health: Women enrolled from 1978 onwards; limited menopause-specific data collected

name: Knight ADRC
full_name: Knight Alzheimer Disease Research Center at WUSTL
n_note: 4,076 at baseline (ADRC + HASD + ACS); 641 active; 1,450 participants with paired CSF and amyloid PET
notes: Deep phenotyping. Rich proteomics (CSF + plasma). Well-curated post-mortem.
ethnic_diversity_note: Predominantly White; (~13%) African American representation at baseline
percent_women_source: Baseline ADRC+HASD+ACS clinical cohort: 2,389/4,076 female (58.6%) ;https://biostat.wustl.edu/adrc/rc_legacy_query/index_02_tab_02_01.php

name: WHICAP
n_note: ~5,000: 4,308 (WHICAP I 1992 + II 1999); +2,128 WHICAP III (2009)[do info if fresh sample or overlap]; MRI subset 1,019; >1,000 actively followed (2021)
notes: Notably diverse cohort: Caribbean Hispanic and African American populations. NYC-based.
ethnic_diversity_note: 1992 follow-up cohort (n=1,788) was 42.5% Caribbean Hispanic, 34.1% African American and 23.4% White, so 76.6% non-White.
percent_women_source: Whole cohort ≈ 68%: 71% of African American, 68% of Caribbean Hispanic and 65% of White participants; MRI subset is 60.8%.

name: ROSMAP
full_name: Religious Orders Study and Memory and Aging Project
notes: Rich post-mortem multi-omics. Unique longitudinal clinical-to-neuropath design.

name: BIOCARD
full_name: Biomarkers of Cognitive Decline Among Normal Individuals
n_note: 456 total (349 original NIH cohort + new enrolment since 2009); ~two-thirds with family history of AD; follow-up up to 27 years
notes: Longitudinal study at Johns Hopkins. About two-thirds have a family history of AD by design, and about a third have since developed MCI or dementia
ethnic_diversity_note: 97.1% Caucasian in the original cohort (n=349). The new cohort “more closely mirrors” population diversity, but no figures are given. Race and Hispanic origin are collected using the standard US NIA categories.
percent_women_source: 58.5 (MRI subset) — https://pennlinc.github.io/AI2D/docs/datasets/BIOCARD

name: NACC
n_note: 217,000+ visits (ranging from 1-20 visits for participants, average of 3.7 visits per participant)
notes: Harmonised data across 40 US Alzheimer's Disease Research Centers. Includes post-mortem neuropathology.
ethnic_diversity_note: Not well documented — includes African American, Hispanic, and Asian minorities across ADRC sites
percent_women_source: AI2D harmonised MRI subset (n=5,004), not whole cohort — https://pennlinc.github.io/AI2D/docs/datasets/NACC
womens_health: UDS v4 form A5/D2, section 7 “Menstrual and reproductive health”, asks why periods stopped (natural menopause or hysterectomy), hormone-replacement use, and birth-control use. Oestradiol is on the medications form (A4).

name: WRAP
n_note: 1,561 enrolled (May 2017), 1,270 active; ~2,000 per WAI (current); 73% with parental history of AD
notes: Prevention-focused registry. 73% have a parental history of AD; 40% carry APOE ε4 (46% with vs 22% without a parental history); ~28% amyloid and/or tau positive
percent_women_source: not clear: a women’s health history questionnaire is part of the protocol, but the paper doesn’t list its variables

name: ADNI
n_note: 2,040 new participants across ADNI1–3 (my sum: ADNI1 819 + ADNI-GO 200 + ADNI2 650 + ADNI3 371). ADNI4 aims for up to 750 new in-clinic participants
notes: Gold-standard AD neuroimaging cohort. Multiple phases (ADNI-1, GO, 2, 3, 4). Predominantly white/European-American.
access_requirements: IDA application + Data Use Agreement, approval = fast
ethnic_diversity_note: ADNI1 was 93% White, 5% Black, 2% Asian, 3% Hispanic. ADNI4 aims for 50–60% of new participants from under-studied populations
percent_women_source: AI2D harmonised MRI subset (n=2,517), not whole cohort — https://pennlinc.github.io/AI2D/docs/datasets/ADNI

name: AddNeuroMed
n_note: 773 AddNeuroMed participants (in ANMerge, 1,702 total); MRI 453; genotyping 1,014; blood transcriptomics 709; plasma proteomics 680 (ANMerge totals)
notes: Pan-European multi-site study. Good geographic diversity within Europe.
access_requirements: Available as part of ANMerge on Synapse: register, submit a short proposal, sign a data use certificate (ethics review), cite ANMerge; approval ~14 days
ethnic_diversity_note: European only; limited diversity within European populations
percent_women_source: ANMerge (harmonised AddNeuroMed), n=1,702: '59% females' — https://atlaslongitudinaldatasets.ac.uk/datasets/anmerge

name: AIBL
full_name: Australian Imaging, Biomarker & Lifestyle Flagship Study
notes: Major Australian cohort. Strong amyloid PET and lifestyle data.
access_requirements: IDA application; also listed on GAAIN (Global Alzheimer’s Association Interactive Network)
percent_women_source: 56.1: AI2D harmonised MRI subset (n=976), not whole cohort — https://pennlinc.github.io/AI2D/docs/datasets/AIBL

name: UK Biobank
n_note: 500,000+ (Update imaging: 100,000 scanned (completed 2025), with 60,000 being re-scanned by 2029)
notes: Population-level biobank. Application-based access. Largest MRI+genetics cohort.
access_requirements: https://www.ukbiobank.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Access-procedures.pdf
percent_women_source: 503,317 recruited 2006–10; '54% of participants are female' — https://www.ukbiobank.ac.uk/about-our-data/our-participants/
womens_health: age at menarche and menopause, number of live births, hysterectomy and/or bilateral oophorectomy (with age), and current/past/never use of hormone therapy and hormonal contraception

name: OASIS-1
full_name: Open Access Series of Imaging Studies — Cross-sectional
notes: Fully open access. Cross-sectional.
access_requirements: Online form with research statement + DUA; institutional email required; non-commercial academic use only; no re-identification or facial reconstruction; acknowledge OASIS.
percent_women_source: Unknown

name: J-ADNI
n_note: 154 cognitively normal, 234 late amnestic MCI, 149 mild AD
notes: Japanese harmonised replication of the ADNI protocol. Enables direct comparison of biomarker profiles between Japanese and North American populations.
percent_women_source: 135/278 participants with amyloid data (Iwatsubo et al. 2018, Table 1; calculated) — https://researchmap.jp/takeshiiwatsubo/published_papers/17234260/attachment_file.pdf

name: MAPT
notes: French multi-domain lifestyle intervention trial in elderly at-risk individuals. Strong data on omega-3 supplementation and cognitive training. 13 sites across France.
percent_women_source: 1,680 randomised; female 1,088 (64.8%) (Vellas et al. 2014)

name: SAGES
full_name: Successful AGing after Elective Surgery — Cognitive Substudy
notes: Longitudinal study examining perioperative cognitive decline. Includes diverse urban Boston population. Notably higher minority representation than most AD cohorts.

name: PREVENT-AD
full_name: Pre-symptomatic Evaluation of Experimental or Novel Treatments for Alzheimer Disease
notes: Focus on individuals at familial risk for AD. Canadian French cohort.
access_requirements: Open: raw MRI (BIDS/MINC) and basic demographics for 308 participants; anyone can request an account. Registered: cognitive, medical, genetic, CSF and lab data for 348 participants; researcher status is verified and access granted on average within a week.
percent_women_source: Open-data subset: 247 women/349 (Tremblay-Mercier et al.; calculated) — https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2020.03.04.976670v2.full-text

name: ADSP
notes: NIH initiative sequencing whole genomes and exomes of AD cases and controls to identify disease-causing and protective variants. Prioritises diverse populations including African American, Hispanic/Latino, and Asian individuals. Data via NIAGADS.

name: ALFA
notes: Catalan cohort of cognitively unimpaired adults, mostly offspring of AD patients. Led by the Barcelona Beta Brain Research Center (BBRC). Strong amyloid/tau PET and CSF biomarker data. ALFA+ sub-study with richer biomarker profiling.
access_requirements: ALFA+ (longitudinal sub-study) data shared since Sept 2026 on the AD Data Initiative's AD Workbench: request via the AD Discovery Portal entry (study description, data dictionary, access form). Free of charge, open to researchers worldwide; governed by a BBRC–AD Data Initiative access model; analysis inside the Workbench (no data transfer). Content: demographics, clinical, cognition, APOE, MRI/PET-derived measures, CSF biomarker status.
percent_women_source: Parent cohort n=2,743: '63.2% were women' (Molinuevo et al. 2016) — https://jcami.eu/documents/The ALFA project. A research platform to identify early pathophysiological features of Alzheimer_s disease. Alzheimer_s _ Dementia.pdf

name: A4 Study
notes: Prevention trial enriched for amyloid positivity. Diverse international sites.
access_requirements: Data shared through LONI IDA: online application and acceptance of the A4 Data Use Agreement.
ethnic_diversity_note: Predominantly White; some diversity across international sites
percent_women_source: n=4,486 screened CN adults, 59% female (Papp et al. 2021, Table 1) — https://escholarship.org/content/qt86b5v6t9/qt86b5v6t9.pdf

name: KBASE
full_name: Korean Brain Aging Study for Early Diagnosis and Prediction of Alzheimer's Disease
notes: First large-scale Korean cohort for AD biomarker research. Critical Asian-population resource for amyloid PET and genetic studies.
percent_women_source: AI2D harmonised MRI subset (n=650), not whole cohort — https://pennlinc.github.io/AI2D/docs/datasets/KBASE

name: EPAD
notes: Prevention-focused. Longitudinal. Multi-modal imaging. European-only.
access_requirements: Final V.IMI dataset (2,096 participants) open since Nov 2020 through the EPAD Research Access Process; data hosted on the AD Data Initiative's AD Workbench (online request); genomic data also on the AD Workbench.
percent_women_source: Baseline release V500.0: 261/500 female (Ritchie et al. 2020) — https://core.ac.uk/download/478175503.pdf

name: DELCODE
full_name: DZNE-Longitudinal Cognitive Impairment and Dementia Study
notes: German prevention study. Subjective cognitive decline enriched. 10 DZNE sites.
access_requirements: Not publicly available; data 'may be provided upon reasonable request' (Jessen et al. 2018 data-availability statement).
percent_women_source: First baseline data n=394: 208 female (Jessen et al. 2018, Table; calculated) — https://epub.ub.uni-muenchen.de/63870/1/63870.pdf

name: Mayo Clinic AD Study
full_name: Mayo Clinic Alzheimer's Disease Genetics Study (AMP-AD)
notes: Part of the AMP-AD consortium. RNA-seq from temporal cortex and cerebellum across AD and control brains. Deposited in Synapse. Complementary to ROSMAP for cross-cohort transcriptomic replication. Carefull with possible overlap
access_requirements: AD Knowledge Portal (Synapse): register and accept the electronic data-use conditions; data dictionary doi:10.7303/syn5478487.2.
age_range_at_entry: ≥50 at death (controls ≥50; AD, PSP, pathologic aging ≥60)
percent_women_source: Temporal-cortex sample, by group: AD and pathologic aging 57%, controls 49%, PSP 39% female (Allen et al. 2016; weighted, calculated) — https://link.springer.com/10.1038/sdata.2016.89

name: MSBB
notes: Multi-region RNA-seq and proteomics from Mount Sinai Brain Bank AD cases and controls. Part of AMP-AD. Includes 4 brain regions per donor, enabling network-based analyses. Available via Synapse.
access_requirements: Available through the AD Knowledge Portal (Synapse, study syn3159438): Synapse account and acceptance of the portal's data-use conditions.
ethnic_diversity_note: Moderate — New York City donor population with some ethnic diversity
percent_women_source: 238 female/364 donors (Wang et al. 2018; calculated) — https://www.nature.com/articles/sdata2018185

name: LASI-DAD
full_name: Longitudinal Aging Study in India — Diagnostic Assessment of Dementia
n_note: GSA array (1008 scans from 993 unique subjects, including 960 LASI - DAD subjects); Neuroimaging data (N=137)
notes: Largest population-based dementia study in India. Critical for LMIC representation.
access_requirements: Register on the Gateway to Global Aging Data and sign a Data Use Agreement before download.
ethnic_diversity_note: Multi-ethnic Indian population across diverse states and linguistic groups
percent_women_source: 2,207/4,096 unweighted (50.8% weighted) (Lee et al. 2023, Table 1) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-023-01941-6.pdf

name: H3Africa Brain
full_name: Human Heredity and Health in Africa — Brain Health
notes: Critical resource for African-descent populations. Addresses the severe gap in sub-Saharan African representation in dementia genetics. Includes genetic data from populations not represented in IGAP or EADB.
access_requirements: H3Africa data are controlled access at the EGA: register on the H3Africa catalogue and submit an online request to the independent Data and Biospecimen Access Committee (DBAC); Data Access Agreement co-signed by the institutional official; DBAC checks bona fide researcher and acceptable use (no scientific review); annual progress reports; publication-embargo rules apply.
ethnic_diversity_note: Sub-Saharan African populations from Ghana, Nigeria, Uganda, Tanzania; among the most underrepresented in AD research

name: OASIS-3
full_name: Open Access Series of Imaging Studies — Longitudinal Neuroimaging, Clinical, and Cognitive Dataset for Normal Aging and Alzheimer Disease
notes: Longitudinal, ~30 years of Knight ADRC data (overlaps Knight ADRC row). 1,378 participants (755 CN, 622 cognitive decline); 2,842 MRI, 2,157 PET (PiB, AV45, FDG), 451 tau PET (OASIS-3_AV1451), 1,472 CT sessions.
access_requirements: NITRC account + institutional email + detailed research statement + DUA; non-commercial academic use only; no third-party sharing; NIH country restrictions (China, Russia, Iran, N. Korea, Cuba, Venezuela); AV45/AV1451 publications reviewed by Avid 30 days before.

name: ReDLat
full_name: Red Latina de Demencias Tempranas (Latin American Network for Early-Onset Dementia)
notes: Crucial for Latin American diversity. Includes Indigenous-descent and mestizo populations.
access_requirements: No data-request procedure published; the consortium planned a harmonised data-sharing platform (Ibanez et al. 2021). Contact the consortium (corresponding author B. L. Miller).
ethnic_diversity_note: Indigenous-descent, mestizo, and mixed populations across 5 Latin American countries

name: ANMerge
notes: Fully open harmonised version of AddNeuroMed. Available via Synapse.
access_requirements: Synapse account + 1–3 paragraph proposal + data use certificate (ethics review) signed by all users; cite ANMerge; approval ~14 days.
percent_women_source: n=1,702: '59% females' — https://atlaslongitudinaldatasets.ac.uk/datasets/anmerge

name: SEA-AD
full_name: Seattle Alzheimer's Disease Brain Cell Atlas
notes: Single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq + ATAC-seq from 84 human brain donors spanning the full AD neuropathological spectrum. Produced by the Allen Institute for Brain Science. Fully open via the Allen Brain Map portal and Synapse.
access_requirements: Processed data open (SEA-AD portal, AWS Open Data); raw data controlled via Synapse (syn26223298). Donor questions: ACT donors KPWA.actproposals@kp.org, UW ADRC donors uwadrc@uw.edu.
percent_women_source: 51 female / 84 donors (Allen Institute, About SEA-AD; calculated) — https://brain-map.org/consortia/sea-ad/about-sea-ad

name: BrainLat
full_name: Latin American Brain Health Institute Neuroimaging Dataset
notes: First open multimodal neuroimaging dataset of neurodegeneration from Latin America. Includes AD, bvFTD, PD, MS and healthy controls. MRI (anatomical, functional, diffusion) + high-density EEG. BIDS format. Hosted on Synapse. Critical resource for underrepresented population neuroscience.

name: Swedish Twin Registry
notes: World's largest twin registry, hosted at Karolinska Institutet. Not primarily designed for AD research — used to disentangle genetic and environmental contributions to dementia through classical twin design.
access_requirements: Applicant must hold a PhD or MD; apply via iLab with a 3–5 page project description, CV and draft ethics application; approval by the Swedish Ethical Review Authority; non-Swedish applicants need a Swedish collaborator. Expert Committee meets 4times/year; access fees apply. Contact str-research@meb.ki.se.

name: Rush MAP
notes: Longitudinal clinical-pathologic cohort from retirement communities in Chicago with brain donation at death. Foundational for linking ante-mortem clinical data to post-mortem neuropathology.
access_requirements: RADC account + signed DUA for de-identified data; omics via AD Knowledge Portal (Synapse) DUA; specimens reviewed by Biospecimen Distribution Committee (merit, funding) + MTA. Fees/timelines not published. MAP is half of ROSMAP (see ROSMAP row, carefull about the overlap).
percent_women_source: AI2D harmonised MRI subset (n=1,183), not whole cohort — https://pennlinc.github.io/AI2D/docs/datasets/MAP-Rush

name: 3C Study
notes: Large French community-based longitudinal cohort across Bordeaux, Dijon, and Montpellier. Investigates the relationship between vascular diseases and dementia. Rich data on vascular risk factors, genetics, and cognitive decline.
access_requirements: Need to send out an email and discuss collaboration
percent_women_source: Analysis sample 3,467 women/5,474 (Grimaud et al. 2013), not full 9,294 baseline — https://rcastoragev2.blob.core.windows.net/a3e8184af24002bcd90b18b8e16831a7/PMC3839909.pdf

name: Sydney MAS
notes: Longitudinal study of community-dwelling older Australians investigating risk factors for MCI and dementia. Includes neuropsychological testing, neuroimaging, genetics, and lifestyle factors.
access_requirements: Data requests through the Dementias Platform Australia (DPAU) Data Portal; https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/dementias-platform/data-portal-supporting-documents/2026-05-data-portal-supporting-documents-compressed.pdf

name: Lifelines
notes: Large multigenerational population-based cohort from the northern Netherlands. Three-generation design covering participants aged 6 months to 93 years. Collects extensive phenotypic, genomic, and lifestyle data with long-term follow-up. Gated access for researchers.
access_requirements: Researchers in or outside the Netherlands submit a research proposal to the Lifelines Research Office; data/biomaterials released for a fee, for scientific research only; analysis in a remote workspace on an HPC cluster.
ethnic_diversity_note: Predominantly White/Dutch; limited diversity due to northern Netherlands geography
percent_women_source: 167,729 participants; '~97,000 female participants (58%)' — https://wiki-lifelines.web.rug.nl/doku.php?id=cohort
womens_health: Menopause status, reproductive history, and hormonal contraceptive use collected

name: BiSC
notes: Exposome birth cohort enrolled October 2018–April 2021 at three Barcelona university hospitals (Hospital Sant Joan de Déu, Hospital de la Santa Creu i Sant Pau, Hospital Clínic). Evaluates socio-environmental and genetic determinants of foetal and child health, growth, and development, as well as maternal mental and physical health during and after pregnancy. Data collected via interviews, questionnaires, home visits, personal sensors, hospital records, ultrasound, MRI, and biological samples. Follow-ups ongoing to 48 months postnatally. Gated data access available.
ethnic_diversity_note: Urban Barcelona population with some ethnic diversity
womens_health: Maternal mental and physical health, pregnancy outcomes, hormonal variables, and reproductive history systematically collected

name: HABS-AD
notes: Longitudinal study at Massachusetts General Hospital investigating the earliest stages of AD in cognitively normal older adults. Emphasises amyloid and tau PET imaging to track preclinical AD trajectories.
access_requirements: Imaging (PET, MRI) and neuropsychological data publicly available on request; requester must agree to a data use agreement; approved requests are listed on the website.
ethnic_diversity_note: 231 white; 45 African American; 6 Asian; 1 Native American
percent_women_source: AI2D harmonised MRI subset (n=289), not whole cohort — https://pennlinc.github.io/AI2D/docs/datasets/HABS

name: MEMENTO
notes: French multi-center cohort of outpatients with subjective cognitive decline (SCD) or mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Recruits from 26 memory clinics across France. Rich multi-modal longitudinal biomarker data.
access_requirements: Not public. Bona fide researchers discuss the idea with the PIs (G. Chêne, C. Dufouil), email an outline to the PIs and the Secretariat, then submit the proposal form (Appendix 1); Scientific coordination committee decides, Steering Committee approves; a contract is needed before analyses; raw MRI/PET images and biological material need specific authorisation. Collaboration with MEMENTO investigators encouraged.
percent_women_source: n=2,323 at baseline: 61.8% women (Dufouil et al. 2017) — https://host.credim.u-bordeaux.fr/dnn-memento/Portals/0/Valorisation/Dufouil_Alz-Res-Ther_2017.pdf

name: B-CUBE
full_name: Bordeaux Cohort for Brain and Cognitive Aging (B-CUBE)
notes: Bordeaux-based longitudinal cohort of 2,000+ volunteers aged 55–80. Investigates the influence of life trajectories and biological factors on health and brain aging.
access_requirements: Not much information

name: All of Us
notes: NIH precision medicine initiative aiming to enroll 1 million+ diverse US participants. Strongly prioritises historically underrepresented populations. Includes EHR, genomics, wearable data, and lifestyle surveys. Researcher access via the Researcher Workbench.
access_requirements: Public tier (aggregate, Data Browser, no login); Registered tier (individual EHR/survey/wearables; workbench registration + data passport); Controlled tier (adds genomic WGS/arrays; extra approval). Project descriptions are made public.
ethnic_diversity_note: >50% participants from underrepresented minorities; explicitly designed for diversity
percent_women_source: 218,981/355,413 female (JAMA Cardiol 2023) — https://www.broadinstitute.org/publications/broad1340556
womens_health: Menstrual history, menopause status, reproductive health, and hormonal variables collected in surveys

name: VIP
full_name: Cognitive Aging Program — Vietnamese American Immigrants
notes: Longitudinal study of cognitive aging in Vietnamese American immigrants, addressing a critically underrepresented population. Not exclusively AD — focuses on cognitive aging with culturally adapted assessments.
access_requirements: No data-availability statement in the cohort description paper; no public access procedure found.
ethnic_diversity_note: Vietnamese American immigrants — a critically underrepresented Asian-American subgroup

name: READD-ADSP
full_name: Recruitment and Retention for Alzheimer's Disease Diversity Genetic Cohorts in the ADSP
notes: Initiative within the Alzheimer's Disease Sequencing Project (ADSP) focused specifically on improving recruitment of underrepresented racial and ethnic groups in AD genetic studies.
access_requirements: Clinical, phenotypic and genetic data to be harmonised with ADGC and ADSP resources (grant aims); no separate access procedure published.
ethnic_diversity_note: 5000 Indigenous Africans, 4000 African Americans, and 4000 Hispanic/Latinix individuals

name: ACAD
notes: Multi-site consortium recruiting individuals of Asian ancestry across North America and Asia. Directly addresses the European-ancestry bias in AD GWAS by studying populations historically excluded from large-scale genomics.
access_requirements: No public data-access procedure found; pilot biosamples deposited at NCRAD.
age_range_at_entry: >60 (cases with cognitive impairment; age- and sex-matched controls)
ethnic_diversity_note: Diverse Asian ancestries (Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Singaporean) across North America and Asia

name: WHIMS
notes: Ancillary study of the WHI hormone therapy trials: double-blind, placebo-controlled test of conjugated equine estrogens (± medroxyprogesterone acetate) on dementia and cognition in women aged 65–79; annual follow-up 1996–2004. WHIMS-MRI sub-study.
access_requirements: Propose a paper or ancillary study through the WHI (whi.org); WHIMS data also documented in NHLBI BioLINCC WHI holdings.
ethnic_diversity_note: WHIMS-Main: 86.4% White, 7.2% Black/African American, 2.6% Hispanic/Latino, 3.7% other
womens_health: Hormone-therapy trial (CEE ± MPA); baseline hysterectomy status and hormone use recorded

name: S3WP
full_name: Swedish SciLifeLab SCAPIS Wellness Profiling study
notes: Longitudinal wellness-profiling sub-study of SCAPIS (Sweden): healthy adults 50–65 with six visits over ~2 years and deep multi-omics profiling.
access_requirements: Participant-level data deposited at the Swedish National Data Service; requests (for validation purposes, subject to Swedish law) to snd@snd.gu.se. Summary statistics in supplements.

name: HUSK
notes: Population-based cohort in Hordaland county, western Norway (Univ. of Bergen / Norwegian Institute of Public Health; part of CONOR). Birth cohorts 1925–27 and 1950–57. In source GWAS: 624 AD cases / 15,329 controls, AD from ICD-10 codes in the Norwegian Patient Registry (2024); genotyped on Illumina GSA v3 at deCODE.
access_requirements: Researchers at institutions with research expertise; online application + project description; REK ethics approval if not covered; reviewed by the Data and Publication Committee (meets ~monthly; submit ≥1 week before); data released after signed agreement. Fees not stated. Contact husk@uib.no. https://husk-en.w.uib.no/files/2024/04/Retningslinjer_april_2023.pdf
percent_women_source: Source GWAS sample: (410 + 8,089)/15,953 (calculated) — Nature 2026 suppl. https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-026-11206-y/MediaObjects/41586_2026_11206_MOESM1_ESM.pdf

name: HUNT
n_note: 3,924 AD cases / 19,410 controls in source GWAS; surveys HUNT1–HUNT4 (1984–2019)
notes: Population-based health surveys of Nord-Trøndelag, Norway, with biobank and national register linkage. AD in source GWAS: ICD-10 G30/F00/F03 (cases diagnosed 40+, controls 70+; ICD-10 data from 1997). Update profile: Åsvold et al. 2023 (doi:10.1093/ije/dyac095).
access_requirements: PhD researchers at Norwegian institutions (foreign researchers only with a Norwegian PI); HUNT databank application + REK approval (+DPIA); Data Access Committee review (~1 month); fees per HUNT price list; manuscripts to HUNT Publication Committee; delete data at project end.

name: 23andMe
notes: Research-consented direct-to-consumer genotyping customers; AD status self-reported. Summary statistics only by application/collaboration. Entered the source GWAS via Wightman et al. 2021.
access_requirements: Summary statistics through the 23andMe Publication Dataset Access Program (application); check current terms after the 2025 ownership change. dataset-request@23andme.com
